data.one_liner: High-performance framework for state, dependency injection, navigation, and translation.
data.what_it_does: SINT provides a micro-framework covering four foundational pillars: reactive state management with signals, contract-first dependency injection, multi-level prefix trie routing, and locale translation caches.
use_when: You want an all-in-one architecture covering state, navigation, dependency injection, and localization without multiple packages.
You need fine-grained reactive signals with batching and computed properties.
You want context-free navigation and dependency resolution bound to route lifecycles.
avoid_when: You prefer strict separation of concerns using independent single-purpose packages.
Your project standardizes on BLoC, Riverpod, or Provider.
You want strictly reactive stream-based architectures.
strengths: Fine-grained $O(1)$ reactive signals with zero-allocation batching and computed properties.
Contract-first dependency injection with automated route-bound lifecycle disposal.
Multi-level prefix trie router for fast route matching.
weaknesses: Monolithic approach tightly couples state, navigation, and DI into a single framework.
Context-free APIs might encourage global state patterns if not carefully managed.
